clue: Letters signed "Senna", 647 to 677, with a hooked correction stroke in the margins
first_reading: A common first name; a schoolmistress's habit
later_meaning: Senna Aldous's own stroke, the one all over the relics
notes: The inciting discovery

clue: A boundary in the letter of 668 that matches the forged entry, not the relic roll
first_reading: A family mistake about the orchard
later_meaning: Only someone who knew the roll before correction could write it
notes: Tamsin notices it as odd in I-05 and does not yet know why

clue: Wexham school record: "Senna, from Calloway, to teach letters", 647, no papers
first_reading: Nothing odd in a dissenting town
later_meaning: A Calloway woman arriving in the spring of the saint's death
notes: Win Corley sees nothing odd in it

clue: The Schoolmistress's Letters, read in the Wexham meeting house
first_reading: Local devotional texts by "a teacher of our town"
later_meaning: The same letters: the dissenters have revered her for three hundred years
notes: Bryony reads one aloud in I-05; the reader hears the voice before Tamsin sees the bundle

clue: Uniform ink and the correction stroke throughout the relic rolls
later_meaning: Copies made in one winter, by Senna
notes: Tamsin passes them every working day

clue: Marit's diary: "S. tired and secret all winter"
later_meaning: The copying
notes: Kate reads it aloud at the Reading as family pride

clue: Dorcas's 660 Account never says Senna died
later_meaning: Dorcas knew she had not
notes: Epigraphs switch to the Account once found

clue: The Great Life's death scene matches Saint Hild of the Door almost line for line
later_meaning: A borrowed death written 150 years later
notes: Plant Hild's legend somewhere ordinary in II (a feast, a statue, a children's play)

clue: Honor Bale's two added lines
later_meaning: A live demonstration that texts grow
notes: The reader hears the lines in I-06 without being told they are new

clue: Tribunal register: "made dead to the Keeping, for the rolls"
first_reading: Read as "died for the rolls" since about 800
later_meaning: A sentence, not a death
notes: The bare phrase "for the rolls" should be on the tomb or in the liturgy before IV

clue: A 690 petition from another woman made dead, asking to be restored
later_meaning: Proves the formula did not mean death

clue: Charge sheet: the evidence of forgery is the copies themselves
later_meaning: The relics were the trial exhibits

clue: Steward's accounts: "B. L., for her word"
later_meaning: The witness was bought
notes: Bett's interlude after III plants the payment without naming anyone

clue: Dorcas's 655 offer and Senna's fair copy of her refusal
later_meaning: Why Senna stayed dead
notes: In the bundle from I-05 but unread until IV; see findings item 5

clue: Marit's 655 petition, "in case she is not dead to me"
where_it_lives: Order archive, filed under "Consolations of the bereaved"
later_meaning: Marit knew she was alive; whether she regretted letting her go is arguable

clue: Translation record: "the grave signed with her hand"
where_it_lives: Order archive; the phrase is carved on the tomb
later_meaning: The stroke on the marker, put there by Senna for someone else
notes: Also the book's title

clue: The bones: a woman of about sixty with a badly healed broken leg
later_meaning: Jory, confirmed by documents, not science alone

clue: Infirmary book, 631: a dyeworks hand, leg broken, discharged unhealed
later_meaning: Jory's leg
notes: Tamsin meets it while tracing Marit's dyeworks for another reason

clue: City fine, 639, for sleeping out
later_meaning: Jory's homelessness
notes: Part of Jory's reconstructed life

clue: Alms book: "Jory of the porch, bread and a blanket", then nothing after spring 647
later_meaning: Jory's death, the week Senna left
notes: Plant in plain sight: a page open in a case in the chapel

clue: Gravestone: "Senna, schoolmistress, kept by those who knew her", 678
later_meaning: The saint's real grave
notes: A set piece: a saint with two graves

clue: The hymn's last line: "Another hand will, another will"
later_meaning: About copying, and about Jory
notes: Juno sings it in I-02

clue: Benedicta's note to Carrow: "the eastern entries, as we discussed"
later_meaning: Benedicta commissioned the forgery, then judged the woman who exposed it

clue: Marit's 661 letter: "The children are well. Wren has your hand. Do not write again."
first_reading: A letter from an unknown M.
later_meaning: Marit knew where Senna was, and chose silence
notes: One letter in the bundle is in another hand, signed M.; Tamsin sets it aside

clue: Taking in, seen at the Reading in Kate's family
later_meaning: How Jory is finally kept without the oath

clue: Marit's diary, among dye orders: spoiled lengths given to the woman on the chapel porch, who "knew the colour by the smell"
later_meaning: Jory knew the Aldous household and had worked with dye, which the infirmary book (C18) later makes her leg
notes: Guardrail: plant the overlooked woman in plain sight. Approved with a refinement (Reuben, 15 Nov): no leg, no vats, no name, so she is available but not salient; the dyeworks link waits for C18

clue: Senna's 645 working notes in the margins of an old survey, citing older surveys
later_meaning: The copies are honest: they match the older surveys against the Order's interest
notes: Disproves Tamsin's Movement III theory

clue: A registrar who brings soup to the porch
later_meaning: Senna fed Jory and is the one who would bury her
notes: The interlude never names Senna and does not say where Jory will be buried
